claims.text: Superconductivity in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by conventional electron–phonon coupling.
Atomic-scale compositional disorder modulates conventional electron–phonon coupling in high-entropy alloys.
Small systematic adjustments in elemental ratios alter the phonon spectrum.
Small systematic adjustments in elemental ratios alter the electronic density of states near the Fermi level.
Composition-induced changes in phonons and the density of states tune the superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed TaNbHfZrTi starting alloy is a single-phase bcc high-entropy alloy after homogenization and uniform heat treatment.
An incremental partial substitution by U or another f-element can be used as the controlled intervention.
The undoped alloy with otherwise identical processing provides the baseline for changes in Tc and electron–phonon coupling.
Local compositional disorder and short-range order directly influence phonon modes.
Local compositional disorder and short-range order directly influence electron-scattering paths.
Increasing elemental disorder changes the electron–phonon coupling parameter.
Increasing elemental disorder changes the density of electronic states at the Fermi level.
Changes in electron–phonon coupling affect Cooper pairing and shift Tc.
Within a limited doping range, f-element substitution will lower Tc if it increases disorder or pair breaking.
If f-element substitution persistently enhances electron–phonon coupling, Tc may rise slightly at an optimum doping level.
At higher doping levels, Tc will eventually saturate or decrease.
Doping above a few atomic percent could induce secondary phases or strong magnetic scattering that masks the electron–phonon-driven response.
Strong spin–orbit coupling can affect superconducting properties in an f-element-containing high-entropy alloy.
The proposed disorder-mediated mechanism may not generalize across different elemental sets or systems with incipient magnetic correlations.
A lack of correlation among doping, local disorder, electron–phonon coupling, and Tc would falsify the proposed disorder-mediated mechanism.

contradictions.description: Introducing an additional element by substitution necessarily changes the total elemental composition, so the instruction to keep the bulk composition constant is not literally compatible unless it means keeping only the host-element ratios and processing constant.
